scientific_hypothesis: A 3-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) dielectric materials on CaF2 substrate can achieve simultaneous high transmittance in both 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands while maintaining strong blocking in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm ranges, within 24-layer constraint.
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS high index contrast reduces required layer count
Evidence demonstrates achievable >83% transmittance in mid-IR
known_risks: Fabrication tolerance may reduce transmittance and increase ripple per evidence
Total thickness may approach stress limits
Dual-band optimization may compromise individual band performance
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase as cavity thicknesses approach half-wave resonance at target wavelengths
tightest_margin should improve as mirror stack reflectivity increases in stopband regions
valid_candidates may decrease if cavity coupling causes unrealistic thickness requirements
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin becomes negative for five consecutive rounds, reduce cavity layer count by one pair and restart optimization
